# synology_firewall (Resource)

Manage the selected DSM firewall profile and its ordered rules. Destroy releases Terraform management and leaves the selected profile and firewall enabled state in place.

## Adopt existing settings

Copy this configuration into a project initialized with [Check the NAS connection](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/elephant-evergreen/synology/latest/docs#check-the-nas-connection). Keep the resource empty to preserve the policy DSM reports. If you change the label `nas`, update the `to` address to match.

```terraform
resource "synology_firewall" "nas" {}

import {
  to = synology_firewall.nas
  id = "firewall"
}
```

1. Run `terraform plan -out=adopt.tfplan`. Expect `1 to import, 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy`. If the plan shows a remote change, stop and check that the resource block is empty and the import ID is `firewall`.
2. Run `terraform apply adopt.tfplan` once the saved plan contains only the import. The next `terraform plan` should report `No changes`.

## Change the firewall policy

Use the [firewall change example and recovery procedure](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/elephant-evergreen/synology/latest/docs/guides/firewall#change-the-selected-profile) after adoption.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `adapters` (Attributes Map) Complete selected-profile policy keyed by DSM adapter name, including global. Rule list order is priority. Omission preserves the observed policy; unknown wire fields fail rather than being discarded. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--adapters))
- `enabled` (Boolean) Enable the selected existing profile. Disabling is explicit and leaves profiles intact.
- `management_networks` (Set of String) Actual administrator source CIDRs as seen by DSM, including any NAT or VPN translation. Required for enabled-policy mutations. These are operator assertions, not automatically discovered addresses; maintain an independent recovery path.
- `port_check_enabled` (Boolean) DSM built-in port checking. Must be true when applying an enabled firewall policy.
- `profile_name` (String) Existing profile to activate. Changing the selection requires enabled = true and an explicit complete adapters policy for review.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Singleton import identity: firewall.
- `management_port` (Number) Observed native DSM HTTPS port. Firewall updates require a direct DSM endpoint whose port matches this value. Matching port numbers do not prove the absence of a proxy or NAT.
- `operation_id` (String) Pending acknowledged DSM firewall-apply task ID, or an empty string after convergence.
- `reconciliation_required` (Boolean) An unfinished or uncertain policy operation is retained. Refresh only polls acknowledged work. Unacknowledged changes require DSM inspection and explicit management release/import.

<a id="nestedatt--adapters"></a>
### Nested Schema for `adapters`

Required:

- `default_policy` (String) Fall-through policy: allow, drop or none. Preserve the imported global policy.
- `rules` (Attributes List) Ordered rules. The first matching rule wins. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--adapters--rules))

<a id="nestedatt--adapters--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `adapters.rules`

Optional:

- `action` (String) Rule action: allow or drop.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Enable this rule.
- `log` (Boolean) Log matching traffic.
- `name` (String) DSM rule description.
- `port_direction` (String) destination or source for custom TCP/UDP ports; empty or destination for all-port rules, empty for ICMP/IGMP rules.
- `port_group` (String) Port selector: all, custom, service or reserved.
- `ports` (String) all, comma-separated ports, one start-end range, or service IDs according to port_group.
- `protocol` (String) Protocol: all, tcp, udp, icmp or igmp.
- `source` (String) all, an IP, address/mask or address/prefix, start-end range, or country codes according to source_group.
- `source_group` (String) Source selector: all, ip, netmask, iprange or geoip.
